# Judith Chapter 4 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Codex Vaticanus, Judith 4 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-DC/JDT_004_page_001.jpg

---

**1** The Israelites of Judea heard what Holofernes had been doing — every temple looted, every nation handed over for destruction. The reports about Nebuchadnezzar's supreme commander reached them in full.

**2** They were terrified. Not just afraid — genuinely terrified. Jerusalem was in danger. The temple of the Lord their God was in danger.

**3** They had only just come home from exile. The people had barely been reassembled. The sacred vessels, the altar, the temple itself had only recently been rededicated after the defilement.

**4** They sent urgent word throughout the region — to Samaria, Kona, Beth-horon, Belmain, Jericho, Choba, Aesora, and the valley of Salem.

**5** They moved fast. They seized the mountain heights, fortified the hilltop villages, and stockpiled provisions for war — the fields had just been harvested, so they had food to work with.

**6** Joakim the high priest, directing affairs from Jerusalem, sent orders to the towns of Bethulia and Betomesthaim — positioned directly across from Esdraelon on the ridge facing Dothan's plain —

**7** telling them to hold the mountain passes at all costs. These passes were the doorways into Judea. The terrain made them defensible: the approach was so narrow that only two men could walk abreast.

**8** The Israelites carried out every order from Joakim and the council of the people assembled in Jerusalem.

**9** And then they prayed. Every man in Israel cried out to God with desperate intensity. They humbled themselves before him with everything they had.

**10** The whole community went into mourning — men, women, children, livestock, resident aliens, hired workers, even the household slaves. All of them put on sackcloth.

**11** Every man, woman, and child in Jerusalem fell prostrate before the temple. They poured ashes on their heads and spread their sackcloth on the ground before the Lord.

**12** They draped the altar itself in sackcloth and raised their voices together in one great cry to the God of Israel: Do not give our children over to plunder. Do not let our wives become war spoil. Do not let the cities we inherited be destroyed. Do not let your sanctuary be desecrated and shamed before the nations.

**13** The Lord heard them. He saw their suffering. The people of Judea and Jerusalem fasted for days before the sanctuary of the Lord Almighty.

**14** Joakim the high priest led the priesthood in mourning. He and every priest who served at the altar and ministered to the Lord kept their sackcloth bound around their waists even as they offered the daily sacrifices, the votive offerings, and the freewill gifts of the people.

**15** Ashes covered their turbans. They cried out to the Lord with all their strength: look with favor on us. Save the whole house of Israel.
